claim: persisted heartbeat Base64 declaration is bounded before owner decode, and stale SHA-normalizing regression source is corrected
findings: The prior snapshot-reader regression expected whitespace-trimmed SHA metadata even though HeartbeatPersistedPollPolicy.Snapshot now retains declared SHA text exactly. The fixture now preserves the whitespace verbatim so future CI cannot accidentally re-authorize integrity normalization.

MAX_PAYLOAD_BASE64_CHARS is derived from OperatorState.MAX_HEARTBEAT_LIGHTS_BYTES using padded Base64 quartet expansion and is enforced by the coherent snapshot reader before OperatorOverlayService decodes the declaration.

The exact-bound fixture proves only reader eligibility. It deliberately does not claim the all-A declaration is canonical Base64 for a maximum-byte payload, accepted integrity, parsed semantics, rendered UI, or delivery.
The reader ceiling bounds decoder input work but cannot prevent SharedPreferences/getAll from materializing an already-corrupt stored String. Do not overclaim it as a persistence-allocation cap.
The separate exact-Base64-canonicality owner patch remains PROPOSED / NOT APPLIED. This pulse did not promote it into owner wiring.
